simple.meaning: מֵידָד (Mêydâd) is a Hebrew word meaning “Medad , an Israelite.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מֵידָד (H4312) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 11:26, with occurrences in Numbers.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֵידָד (H4312) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מֵידָד (H4312) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מֵידָד (Mêydâd) / H4312 is traced through Numbers 11:26, Numbers 11:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad; and the Spirit rested on them. They were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp.

timeline.evidenceText: But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad; and the Spirit rested on them. They were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp.
